description: Core shikigami (summon) definition: Blueprint, action controller, stats, cooldowns, linked animation/material/effect/sound/unique rows and auto-attack ranges.

ID.technical: FName row key reached through joins CharacterShikigami.Id_Shikigami[] -> ShikigamiDataTables (+0x6C0) in battle preload/spawn/sequencer; capture paths use CharacterCaptureRow.Id_ShikigamiCharacter. The first table containing the ID wins; missing rows abort ResolveRows or are skipped depending on the caller. 20 exported rows (CN_010 ... CN_280 family).

FileName_BP.technical: FName primary-asset loader key (export rows are <ID>_BP, e.g. CN_010_00_BP). Battle preload appends it to the shikigami asset list; capture setup resolves it via Slot.ShikigamiLoaders.FindChecked (a missing loader is fatal there). Used with GamePrimaryAssetType_Shikigami.

Id_ShikigamiMaterial.simple: ShikigamiMaterialDataTable row ID for material patterns.
Id_ShikigamiMaterial.technical: FName; resolved on demand by the shikigami material controller when a pattern is applied, via ShikigamiMaterialDataTables (+0x6D0). None/missing rows leave materials unchanged. Export values are None for most rows and e.g. CN_040 where patterns exist.

Id_ShikigamiAnimation.simple: List of ShikigamiAnimationDataTable sets to load/use.
Id_ShikigamiAnimation.technical: TArray<FName> of animation-set IDs. Battle preload appends each set's FileName array to the AnimMontage preload list; battle spawn resolves each set and calls AnimInstance.SetAnimationAsset for its Key/FileName pairs. Export CN_010 uses CN_010 (base), CN_010_DAMAGE and per-attack sets with None padding.

ActionControllerType.simple: Enum selecting the shikigami's action controller class.
ActionControllerType.technical: EGameShikigamiActionControllerType (e.g. CN_010) passed to AGameShikigami::CreateActionController and CreateBoneController at spawn. Failure to create either aborts shikigami initialization. Export rows carry the matching CN_xxx enum value.

SummonCursedEnergyLevel.simple: Minimum caster cursed-energy level to summon.
SummonCursedEnergyLevel.technical: int32 compared with OwnerCharacter.StatusController.GetCursedEnergyLevelClamped(); when the row value is greater, AGameShikigami::IsSummonAvailable returns false before the summon-cooldown check. Export CN_010 uses 1.

HitPoint.technical: float copied to both HitPointMax and HitPoint by UGameShikigamiStatusController::ApplyHitPointParameters (retail 0x1414952E0); subsequent damage changes the current value. Export CN_010=120.0.

DownValue.simple: Shikigami down/daze gauge maximum and initial value.
DownValue.technical: float copied to DownValueMax and DownValue by ApplyDownValueParameters (retail 0x1414952A0); damage reduces DownValue until it reaches zero and the shikigami goes down. Export CN_010=150.0.

OrderCoolTime.simple: Cooldown between player orders to the shikigami.
OrderCoolTime.technical: float seconds copied to StatusController.OrderCoolTime at setup and reset by shikigami actions (row +0x40); CP_030/CP_240 order actions copy it into the status timer (Unknown98) to gate further orders. Export CN_010=0.3.

SummonCoolTime.simple: Cooldown before the shikigami can be summoned again.
SummonCoolTime.technical: float seconds copied to StatusController.SummonCoolTime at setup; actions set SummonCoolTimeLeft from it, and UI widgets display the remaining ratio SummonCoolTimeLeft/SummonCoolTime. Export CN_010=16.0.

bIsInstanceDeathEnabled.simple: Whether this summon can die as an instance.
bIsInstanceDeathEnabled.technical: bool returned by AGameShikigami::IsInstanceDeathEnabled (retail 0x1488820, row +0x48); the flag is consumed through the actor interface, so the actual death/cleanup decision is in callers outside this table's code. Export rows all false.

bImmortalityEnabled.simple: Whether the shikigami is immune to normal defeat.
bImmortalityEnabled.technical: bool checked at the start of AGameShikigami::IsDefeated (retail 0x1488350): when true, defeat is driven solely by bRequestedActive instead of StatusController hit points. Export rows all false.

AutoAttackDistance_Owner.simple: Maximum distance from the summoner for auto-attack.
AutoAttackDistance_Owner.technical: float UE units; GetAutoAttackDistanceOwner returns it (retail 0x14147FF20) and shikigami action AI compares the distance between shikigami and OwnerCharacter against it before auto-attacking. Export CN_010=1800.0.

AutoAttackDistance_Target.simple: Maximum distance to the target for auto-attack.
AutoAttackDistance_Target.technical: float UE units; GetAutoAttackDistanceTarget returns it (retail 0x14147FF30) and the action AI compares shikigami-to-target distance against it (inverted comparison in the source; NaN counts as in range). Export CN_010=2500.0.

Id_ActionMove.technical: FName; when non-None, ResolveRows looks it up in ActionMoveDataTables and caches MoveRow; a missing row aborts setup while None keeps the previous row. Shikigami action code reads cached MoveRow thereafter.

Id_ActionJump.technical: FName; same lookup/cache pattern as Id_ActionMove over ActionJumpDataTables (cached JumpRow, +0x5D0); missing non-None rows abort setup.

Id_ActionDash.technical: FName; same lookup/cache pattern over ActionDashDataTables (cached DashRow, +0x5E0); missing non-None rows abort setup. Export CN_010 uses CN_010.

Id_CharacterEffect.simple: CharacterEffectDataTable row for shikigami visual effects.
Id_CharacterEffect.technical: FName resolved through Shikigami_FindRow over CharacterEffectDataTables (+0x4D0) and cached as EffectRow during ResolveRows; that row's FileName_BP list feeds preload. None yields no effect row. Most exported shikigami rows use None.

Id_CharacterSound.technical: FName resolved via Shikigami_FindCharacterSoundRow (retail 0x14147E710) over CharacterSoundDataTables (+0x510), with bCheckNone=true, and cached as SoundRow. Export rows are mostly None.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.simple: Voice group for generic shikigami actions.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_DefaultAction.technical: FName (row +0x7C) resolved to a ShikigamiVoiceGroupDataTable row in PlayVoice case 1; the group's Id_VoiceGroup[Value] selects the cue without a bounds check (Value used directly). Any non-None voice group field also enables shikigami battle voice playback via SetBattleVoiceEnabled.

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Attack.technical: FName (row +0x84) resolved in PlayVoice case 3; requires Value>0 and indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value-1].

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Damage.simple: Voice group for shikigami damage reactions.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Damage.technical: FName (row +0x8C) resolved in PlayVoice case 6; requires Value>0 and indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value-1].

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Down.simple: Voice group for shikigami down/damage states.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Down.technical: FName (row +0x94) resolved in PlayVoice case 8; indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value] directly (no bounds check).

Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Unique.simple: Voice group for shikigami unique actions.
Id_ShikigamiVoiceGroup_Unique.technical: FName (row +0x9C) resolved in PlayVoice case 10; indexes Id_VoiceGroup[Value] directly (no bounds check).

Id_ShikigamiUnique.technical: TArray<FName>; ResolveRows resolves each ID against ShikigamiUniqueDataTables (+0x700) into UniqueRows. Consumers then use GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(ValueIndex, RowIndex) with the array position as RowIndex. Export CN_010 has base and per-attack entries with None padding.

FootIKLimit.simple: Foot IK reach limits for the shikigami's bone controller.
FootIKLimit.technical: TArray<double> (export CN_010 has 4 values, all 0.0 for that row) passed as the FootIKLimit pointer to CreateBoneController(ActionControllerType, FootIKLimit) at spawn; per-character bone controllers read elements (usually [0] and sometimes [1]) into limb IK Limit fields. The array is stored in the row without a BlueprintReadWrite specifier in the reconstructed header.

notes: ShikigamiDataTables is manager slot +0x6C0; the name is registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:410 and resolved at line 238. CharacterShikigamiDataTable (+0x4F0) is the per-character selection table that points here.

ResolveRows is mostly fail-fast: missing rows for Id_ActionMove/Jump/Dash leave previously cached rows in place but abort setup, while None IDs are skipped. Id_CharacterEffect/Id_ShikigamiUnique tolerate None with bCheckNone behavior of the shared finders.
The 20 exported rows share the same schema; no localization variants or numbered shards exist in this table (ShikigamiVoiceGroup and ShikigamiUnique are separate tables).
Voice-group indexing conventions are per-event and unchecked; consult ShikigamiVoiceGroupDataTable for the Id_VoiceGroup arrays.

usages.detail: Battle preload joins CharacterShikigami -> Shikigami rows, collecting FileName_BP plus all referenced animation filenames.
ResolveRows caches ActionMove/Jump/Dash, unique, effect and sound rows for the spawned shikigami.
Spawn creates the action and bone controllers from ActionControllerType and FootIKLimit.
Initializes HP/down gauges and summon/order cooldowns from the row.
Auto-attack AI checks owner/target distance limits from the row.
PlayVoice resolves the five voice group IDs into ShikigamiVoiceGroup rows and indexes their cue arrays.
